000
FXUS63 KIWX 241905
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
205 PM EST Tue Nov 24 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Increasing clouds today which stick around through at least
  Friday. High temperatures will be in the 40s this week.

- A period of soaking rain arrives early Thursday morning and
  lingers through Friday (80-90% chance). A few snowflakes may
  mix in Thursday night.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 152 PM EST Tue Nov 24 2026

Dry conditions will persist through most of the day Wednesday
due to high pressure over the Midwest. It will be cold tonight
with lows in the mid 20s but mild tomorrow with highs in the 
mid 40s. A vigorous weather system will also start moving up 
into the region on Wednesday evening, bringing breezy east winds
and rain into the southwest portion of the forecast area. Rain 
will then overspread the area on Thanksgiving, with locations 
south of US30 seeing an inch or more of water. A few snowflakes 
could mix in Thursday night, but confidence is low that there 
will be any accumulations since surface temperatures should 
remain above freezing. Showers will diminish on Friday as the 
moves into New England. 

Drier conditions can be expected Saturday and Sunday, although 
a series of weaker shortwaves could bring light precip at times,
with the best chances on Sunday afternoon. DRy, zonal flow is 
expected Monday, and possible Tuesday. Although the GFS does 
bring another wet shortwave into the region Tuesday afternoon. 
Temperatures will remain near to above normal going into the 
beginning of December with highs in the mid to upper 40s.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z TAFS THROUGH 18Z WEDNESDAY/...
Issued at 1118 AM EST Tue Nov 24 2026

Quiet, dry weather continues through the TAF forecast period as
surface high pressure presides over the Midwest. Winds will
remain very consistent out of the northeast at around 5-10 kts.
Visible satellite imagery shows lake effect cloud cover
streaming into northern Indiana off of Lake Michigan; additional
high clouds are expected to arrive tonight from the west ahead
of our next weather system set to bring a soggy Thanksgiving.
VFR conditions prevail through the TAF forecast period.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Cobb
AVIATION...Johnson

spc.text:
SPC AC 241948

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0148 PM CST Tue Nov 24 2026

   Valid 242000Z - 251200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms are not forecast across the contiguous United
   States through tonight.

   ...20z Update...
   Only minor changes were made to the existing general thunder areas
   with this update based on latest observations and guidance trends.
   While increasing thunderstorm coverage remains expected late tonight
   across the Keys/South FL, the overall severe potential continues to
   appear too low to warrant the inclusion of low severe probabilities
   at this time. See the previous discussion for additional details.

   Elsewhere, isolated lightning flashes may occur across portions of
   coastal northern California as a low-topped line of convection moves
   ashore later this evening in tandem with an approaching mid/upper
   trough; however, forecast sounding profiles suggest that overall
   coverage of lightning is likely to remain less than 10%.

   ..Chalmers.. 11/24/2026

   .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1008 AM CST Tue Nov 24 2026/

   ...Synopsis and Discussion...
   Upper troughing over the central CONUS will further amplify through
   the period as multiple embedded mid-level shortwave troughs advance
   east-southeastward across the northern/central Plains and the
   southern High Plains to the lower MS Valley, respectively. A prior
   frontal intrusion well into the Gulf will greatly limit low-level
   moisture and thunderstorm potential for a large majority of the
   CONUS through tonight, with a few exceptions. Elevated thunderstorms
   should continue for a few more hours late this morning into the
   early afternoon across coastal/south TX. Additional elevated
   convection may occur this evening/overnight over portions of the
   central Gulf Coast states, but MUCAPE is forecast to remain weak
   across this region.

   Increasing thunderstorm coverage is expected late tonight into early
   Wednesday morning across the Keys/south FL, as a weak
   southern-stream mid-level perturbation moves over the eastern Gulf.
   Low/mid-level flow should remain modest (generally 25 kt or less)
   per latest RAP forecast soundings, with poor lapse rates aloft also
   present. Accordingly, the overall severe potential across the
   Keys/south FL through the end of the period (25/12Z) still appears
   too limited to include low probabilities at this time.

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 0100Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 241718

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1118 AM CST Tue Nov 24 2026

   Valid 251200Z - 261200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS OVER THE FLORIDA
   KEYS AND SOUTHERN FLORIDA PENINSULA...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Isolated severe storms capable of damaging winds and perhaps a brief
   tornado or waterspout appear possible over the Florida Keys and
   southern Florida peninsula on Wednesday.

   ...Synopsis...

   A short-wave trough initially from the Ozark Plateau into the
   western Gulf at 12Z Wednesday is forecast to intensify into a
   negatively tilted system over the Southeast Wednesday night into
   early Thursday morning. Ahead of that feature, a weaker,
   low-latitude disturbance will move through the central and southern
   FL peninsula Wednesday morning. In the low levels, a surface cyclone
   is expected to progress through the FL Keys and southern FL
   peninsula on Wednesday along a poleward-advancing warm front moving
   into the those areas. The surface low is forecast to undergo more
   significant deepening Wednesday night as it moves onshore in eastern
   NC.  

   ...Florida Keys and southern Florida peninsula...

   Strengthening low-level warm advection and midlevel height falls
   preceding the lower-latitude disturbance are expected to result in
   considerable thunderstorm development Wednesday morning in the
   vicinity of the surface low and retreating warm front. However, the
   influx of boundary-layer dewpoints in the low 70s F south of the
   front will support modest air mass destabilization by afternoon with
   MLCAPE generally less than 1000 J/kg. At the same time, a gradual
   strengthening of the low/midlevel wind field is forecast with the
   approach of the primary upper-air system. As such, the environment
   may become supportive of transient supercell structures embedded
   within the broader convective regime Wednesday afternoon. A
   2-percent tornado probability has been included in this forecast
   update to account for the potential for a brief tornado and/or
   waterspout, in additional to locally damaging outflow winds.


   ...Eastern North Carolina and the Outer Banks...

   Model differences exist in the track of the deepening surface low,
   which is forecast to move onshore Wednesday night into early
   Thursday. Both low-level moisture and vertical shear will increase
   along and east of the surface low track, which could lead to some
   brief tornado and/or damaging wind risk developing toward the end of
   the forecast period. While confidence in that threat is currently
   too low to include severe weather probabilities with this forecast
   issuance, model trends will be monitored for a possible addition in
   subsequent Day 1 outlooks.

   ..Mead.. 11/24/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 0700Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 241916

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0116 PM CST Tue Nov 24 2026

   Valid 261200Z - 271200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are unlikely on Thursday through Thursday night.

   ...Synopsis...

   A negatively tilted short-wave trough is forecast to pivot
   north-northeast along the Atlantic Coast in advance of an intense
   mid/upper-level low, which will progress from the Mid-South into the
   central Appalachians. Elsewhere, a short-wave trough and associated
   mid/upper-level wind maxima will advance from the vicinity of the
   Pacific Northwest and BC coasts into the northern High Plains. At
   the surface, 12Z deterministic and 06Z ensemble model data depict
   varying tracks of a surface low from eastern NC into the southern
   Mid-Atlantic on Thursday, which in turn has implications for the
   extent of onshore moistening and destabilization near and east of
   that feature.


   ...Eastern North Carolina into Southern New England...

   Strong warm advection and midlevel height falls preceding the lead
   upper-air disturbance will contribute to at least isolated
   thunderstorms embedded within a broader precipitation shield. 12Z
   REFS guidance is suggestive that surface-based instability will
   largely remain offshore with storms likely being elevated within a
   strongly sheared but only marginally unstable, weak-lapse-rate
   environment. However, a couple of AI-based systems do indicate low
   severe weather probabilities from eastern NC to along the
   Mid-Atlantic coast on Thursday. That being said, sub-5-percent
   severe probabilities will be maintained with this forecast update
   due to uncertainties in the degree of inland destabilization for
   surface-based parcels.

   Elsewhere, isolated thunderstorms appear possible over western WA on
   Thursday within a zone of strong dynamic cooling/lift coincident
   with the left exit region of the mid/upper-level jet.

   ..Mead.. 11/24/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
